entries.title: Brief · Live systems on the site
entries.text: - Strategy Lab (/lab/): his research sandbox on weekly ETF prices from Dec 2015 to Sep 2026 (SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, AGG, TLT, GLD, VNQ). Signals use data up to week t and earn week t+1 (tested for look-ahead); trading costs are modelled; prices exclude dividends. It is hypothetical research, not a live trading system; no capital is managed with it. - Strategy Lab research, online portfolio selection: he implemented algorithms from the Li & Hoi survey (EG, PAMR, OLMAR, uniform CRP) and stress-tested a claim from academic work, including a NYU Stern Glucksman Fellowship study, that mean-reversion algorithms such as PAMR deliver outstanding wealth. Frictionless, it replicates: PAMR compounded 10.5% a year vs 7.6% for equal weight. But PAMR trades about 55.4% of the portfolio every week; its edge is gone by 5 bps of cost and out of sample (May 2021 to Sep 2026, 10 bps) it earned 0.8% a year. Exponentiated Gradient was the most robust: about 0.3% weekly turnover, edge intact at 50 bps. - Strategy Lab Monte Carlo: 1,000 bootstrapped ten-year paths. No strategy reliably beat the S&P 500 on return (at most a few percent of paths). The defensive rules reliably cut drawdowns: 60/40 had a shallower drawdown than the S&P 500 in 99.8% of paths, volatility targeting in 91.5%, inverse volatility in 96.2%. That is the honest result: these rules trade return for smaller drawdowns; they do not have a high probability of outperforming. - Deal Lab (/deal/) and Wholesale Deal Analyzer v2 (Excel): his Ohio wholesale real-estate analyzer, audited and rebuilt. v1 left the end buyer's selling, closing and holding costs out, never applied its own 15% rehab contingency, and used a 15% buyer-margin test while its note said 20%. On v1's own example (ARV $160,000, rehab $40,000, contract $60,000) v1 said GO; v2 says NO-GO: the true maximum allowable offer is $56,000 and the buyer's margin is 17.5%. A 1,000-trial Monte Carlo in the workbook, cross-checked against a 200,000-trial Python simulation, puts the chance the deal closes at a profit near 29%. - Twin-Engine: a concept family-office dashboard for a two-market real-estate platform (US buy-fix-rent-refinance and India flips) with a Clean Books compliance index. The data in it is illustrative sample data, not real holdings. He rebuilt it so every figure is computed from the records. - Sentinel: research on AI-failure losses: 29 public loss claims graded A to D by source quality, a 60,000-trial Monte Carlo of strategy viability and a 400,000-simulation pricing model. Code is private; a walkthrough is available on request. - Research HQ (/research/) and the research city on the home page: each project is drawn as a building whose lit floors are shipped milestones and whose scaffolding is unfinished work; each bot is a real automated job (a scheduled search, a CI test run, a release gate or a reproducible script). It also has a knowledge graph of his research vault: Obsidian notes in four folders (core theses, data pipelines, models and simulations, peer-review logs of mistakes he caught and fixed). - The Brain: a self-improving strategy search that runs every 6 hours on GitHub Actions at no cost. It mutates the Strategy Lab's rule families, backtests children on Jan 2016 to May 2021 data only, scores them out of 100 (risk-adjusted return, fold consistency, drawdown, costs, robustness), and promotes a challenger only if it beats the champion on more folds than it loses (Elo-rated) with a higher score. Scores are discounted with the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado), which grows stricter with every strategy tried. May 2021 to Sep 2026 is a locked holdout it never sees; a test scrambles those prices and proves its choices do not change. Holdout results are reported for the champion only. Caveats he states himself: choosing the eight ETFs in 2026 is itself hindsight, and the search uses no language model; mutations are parametric, so runs are free and reproducible. The live generation, champion and log are on /research/#brain; it is research, not a trading system. - High Properties: a lead-generation web platform for a real-estate business (Vercel, Supabase, WhatsApp follow-up). The code is public on his GitHub.

entries.title: Research note · 00_CORE_THESES/Costs kill mean reversion
entries.text: # Costs kill mean reversion **Claim.** Online portfolio selection's headline winners (PAMR, OLMAR) earn their edge by trading most of the book every week. Once you pay for that trading, the edge is gone. **Evidence.** In [[OPS replication]], PAMR compounds at 10.5% a year with zero costs but turns over about 55% of the portfolio weekly. The [[Cost sweep]] puts its break-even at about 5 bps per side. Out of sample at 10 bps it earns 0.8% a year, against 12.1% for holding SPY. **Status.** Supported. Prior work: [[Li & Hoi survey]], [[Lahanis, Liu & Zhou]].

entries.title: Research note · 00_CORE_THESES/Defense over offense
entries.text: # Defense over offense **Claim.** Simple defensive rules do not reliably beat an equity index on return. What they reliably do is lose less in bad markets. **Evidence.** Across 1,000 ten-year [[Block bootstrap Monte Carlo]] paths, no rule beats SPY's return reliably, but the 60/40 mix has a shallower worst drawdown than SPY in 99.8% of paths, inverse volatility in 96% and volatility targeting in 92%. See [[Strategy Lab rules]]. **Why it matters.** For a family that thinks in decades, avoiding the drawdown that forces a sale matters more than the last point of return.

entries.title: Research note · 00_CORE_THESES/Evidence over assertion
entries.text: # Evidence over assertion **Claim.** A model is only as credible as its least-checked number. Every figure should be generated by code and asserted by a test, never typed. **Where it shows.** [[Sentinel pricing model]] fails its build if a figure is hand-typed (332 assertions). [[Twin-Engine metrics]] replaced a typed IRR with computed figures, see [[Twin-Engine audit]]. The Strategy Lab tests for look-ahead on every release.

entries.title: Research note · 00_CORE_THESES/Search needs a locked holdout
entries.text: # Search needs a locked holdout **Claim.** An automated search over strategies will always find something that looks good in-sample. The defence is a holdout the search never sees, plus a statistic that charges for every trial. **Implementation.** The [[Brain evolution loop]] selects on 2016–2021 data only; a test scrambles every post-2021 price and proves nothing it chooses changes. Scores are discounted by the [[Deflated Sharpe ratio]], which grows stricter as the trial count grows. **Known weakness.** Choosing the eight ETFs in 2026 is itself hindsight. A champion that beats SPY out of sample is evidence, not proof.

entries.title: Research note · 00_CORE_THESES/Underwrite the buyer
entries.text: # Underwrite the buyer **Claim.** A wholesale assignment only closes if the end buyer still makes money after their own selling, closing and holding costs. A deal that clears the 70% rule can still be a NO-GO. **Evidence.** The example deal in [[Deal Analyzer v2]] clears v1's checks but leaves the buyer a 17.5% margin against a 20% minimum once buyer costs are counted. The [[Deal Monte Carlo]] says it works in about 29% of outcomes. Found in [[Deal Analyzer v1 audit]].

entries.title: Research note · 01_DATA_PIPELINES/Deal inputs
entries.text: # Deal inputs ARV, rehab, contingency, assignment fee, earnest money, marketing spend, buyer cost rate, minimum buyer margin and close rate. Example values come from the v1 workbook's own example deal so the audit compares like with like. Uncertainty for the [[Deal Monte Carlo]]: ARV σ 8%, rehab overrun 10% ± 15%. These are assumptions, not market estimates; comps should replace them. Used by [[Deal Analyzer v2]].

entries.title: Research note · 01_DATA_PIPELINES/Sentinel loss claims
entries.text: # Sentinel loss claims 29 public claims of losses caused by AI failures, each graded A–D by source quality before it can feed a number. Low-grade claims are kept for context but excluded from the base case. Feeds [[Sentinel pricing model]].

entries.title: Research note · 01_DATA_PIPELINES/Weekly ETF bars
entries.text: # Weekly ETF bars - **Assets:** SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, AGG, TLT, GLD, VNQ - **Span:** 561 weekly bars, 2015-12-28 → 2026-09-21 - **Source:** Robinhood market data, split-adjusted closes - **Left out:** distributions (dividends and bond coupons). This understates bond-heavy rules most. - **Split:** selection to 2021-05-10, holdout after Feeds [[Strategy Lab rules]], [[OPS replication]], [[Block bootstrap Monte Carlo]] and the [[Brain evolution loop]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Block bootstrap Monte Carlo
entries.text: # Block bootstrap Monte Carlo 1,000 ten-year paths built by resampling whole weeks of all eight assets at once, in blocks of geometric length (mean 8 weeks), seed 20261006. Keeps cross-asset correlation and volatility clustering. Method: [[Politis & Romano 1994]]. Reports, per rule: CAGR, drawdown and Sharpe quantiles, and the probability of beating SPY on return, Sharpe and Calmar, or of a shallower drawdown. Result: [[Defense over offense]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Brain evolution loop
entries.text: # Brain evolution loop Runs every 6 hours on GitHub Actions at no cost. 1. **Mutate.** Pick a hypothesis family by UCB1 and mutate its best genome (windows, assets, rebalance interval, target volatility, weights). 12% of children are random restarts. 2. **Execute.** Backtest on the selection window only: the code passes a sliced copy of [[Weekly ETF bars]]. 3. **Evaluate.** Rubric out of 100: risk-adjusted return 30, fold consistency 20, drawdown 20, costs 10, robustness 20 ([[Deflated Sharpe ratio]]). 4. **Rate.** Play the challenger against the champion on four folds with Elo updates. Promotion needs more fold wins than losses, a higher score, a drawdown above −35% and cost drag under 1.5% a year. 5. **Remember.** Log why each loser lost; turnover or drawdown failures bias the next mutations (slower rebalancing, more defensive settings). Step sizes follow Rechenberg's 1/5 success rule. Holdout results are reported for the champion only. Thesis: [[Search needs a locked holdout]]. Inspired by autonomous research loops: [[Autonomous research loops]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Cost sweep
entries.text: # Cost sweep Full-sample CAGR of each [[OPS replication]] rule at 0, 5, 10, 25 and 50 bps per side. PAMR and OLMAR break even at about 5 bps; EG survives past 50 bps because it barely trades. Supports [[Costs kill mean reversion]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Deal Analyzer v2
entries.text: # Deal Analyzer v2 MAO = ARV × 70% − rehab × (1 + contingency) − fee. Buyer all-in = contract + fee + rehab with contingency + buyer costs. Signal requires contract ≤ MAO, buyer margin ≥ minimum and positive expected profit (close-rate weighted). The workbook and the web model tie to the cent; the release checks enforce it. Inputs: [[Deal inputs]]. Risk: [[Deal Monte Carlo]]. History: [[Deal Analyzer v1 audit]]. Thesis: [[Underwrite the buyer]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Deal Monte Carlo
entries.text: # Deal Monte Carlo 5,000 draws of ARV and rehab overrun; a deal "works" if the buyer's margin clears the minimum and it closes. The example deal works in about 29% of outcomes (Excel 29.5%, Python 29.3%). A solver finds the highest contract price that works 60% of the time. Part of [[Deal Analyzer v2]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Deflated Sharpe ratio
entries.text: # Deflated Sharpe ratio The probability that a strategy's true Sharpe ratio beats what the best of N unskilled strategies would show by luck, adjusting for skew, fat tails and sample length. N is every strategy the [[Brain evolution loop]] has ever tried, so the bar rises as the search runs. Source: [[Bailey & López de Prado 2014]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/OPS replication
entries.text: # OPS replication Uniform constant rebalancing (UCRP), Exponentiated Gradient (EG), PAMR and OLMAR, with the hindsight-optimal BCRP as an oracle. Parameters are chosen on the selection window and frozen for the holdout. | Rule | 0 bps CAGR | Weekly turnover | Holdout CAGR at 10 bps | |---|---|---|---| | PAMR | 10.5% | 55% | 0.8% | | OLMAR | 9.3% | 55% | 0.4% | | EG | — | 0.3% | 6.1% | | SPY | — | — | 12.1% | See [[Cost sweep]]. Tests [[Costs kill mean reversion]]. Prior work: [[Li & Hoi survey]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/S&P Global DCF

Landed within 10% of analyst consensus. The home page's Model station is a live version of the sensitivity grid. Follows [[Evidence over assertion]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Sentinel pricing model
entries.text: # Sentinel pricing model Frequency-severity simulation for AI-liability cover (400,000 simulations) and a 60,000-trial viability model. Inputs: [[Sentinel loss claims]]. The build fails if any figure is typed rather than generated (332 assertions). Thesis: [[Evidence over assertion]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Strategy Lab rules
entries.text: # Strategy Lab rules Six weekly, long-only rules with no leverage and no look-ahead: buy & hold, strategic mix (60/40), trend filter, dual momentum, inverse volatility and volatility target. A signal formed on week t's close earns week t+1's return; a test tampers with future prices and checks that past weights do not move. Data: [[Weekly ETF bars]]. Stress-tested in [[Block bootstrap Monte Carlo]]. Searched automatically by the [[Brain evolution loop]].

entries.title: Research note · 02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/Twin-Engine metrics
entries.text: # Twin-Engine metrics Equity by market, gross value-add, realised exit multiple, renovation share and compliance, all computed from the property records. IRR is left blank until there are dated cash flows to compute it from. Runs on illustrative sample data. See [[Twin-Engine audit]].

entries.title: Research note · 03_PEER_REVIEW_LOGS/2026-10 OPS review
entries.text: # 2026-10 · OPS review **Attempted.** Replicate the paper's ranking of online portfolio selection rules. **What went wrong.** At zero cost the replication agreed with the paper, and that agreement was the trap: the ranking reverses once trades cost money. **Fix.** Report every rule across a [[Cost sweep]], freeze parameters before the holdout, and lead with the cost-adjusted result. See [[OPS replication]].

entries.title: Research note · 03_PEER_REVIEW_LOGS/2026-10 Webhook incident
entries.text: # 2026-10 · Webhook incident **What happened.** The portfolio's Google Sheets webhook wrote a plain number into a People CRM column that an ARRAYFORMULA fills, which blocked the formula and showed #REF!. **Root cause.** The writer only skipped cells that held a formula themselves; cells filled by an array formula look empty. **Fix.** Any column with a formula below its header is now read-only to the webhook, with a test that reproduces the original sheet layout. Same principle as [[Evidence over assertion]]: test against the real layout, not an idealised one.

entries.title: Research note · 03_PEER_REVIEW_LOGS/Deal Analyzer v1 audit
entries.text: # Deal Analyzer v1 audit **Bugs found.** 1. Rehab contingency recommended but never applied. 2. End buyer's selling, closing and holding costs missing from their margin. 3. Two minimum margins (15% in the signal, 20% in the guidance). 4. Return on cash ignored marketing spend. 5. Expected profit ignored the close rate. **Effect.** The example deal flipped from GO to NO-GO. **Fixed in** [[Deal Analyzer v2]].

entries.title: Research note · 03_PEER_REVIEW_LOGS/Twin-Engine audit
entries.text: # Twin-Engine audit **Found.** A 16.8% IRR typed into the dashboard with nothing behind it; negative currency displayed wrong; no "rented" status; sold properties had no stage; sample data unlabelled. **Fixed.** All figures computed in [[Twin-Engine metrics]]; IRR left blank until it can be computed; sample data labelled illustrative.

entries.title: Research note · 04_REFERENCES/Autonomous research loops
entries.text: # Autonomous research loops The propose → evaluate → keep-or-roll-back pattern of autonomous research agents, such as Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch and open-source self-evolving agent frameworks. The [[Brain evolution loop]] uses the pattern without a language model: mutations are parametric, so every run is free, deterministic and auditable.

entries.title: Research note · 04_REFERENCES/Bailey & López de Prado 2014
entries.text: # Bailey & López de Prado 2014 David H. Bailey and Marcos López de Prado, "The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality", *Journal of Portfolio Management* (2014). Used in [[Deflated Sharpe ratio]].

entries.title: Research note · 04_REFERENCES/Lahanis, Liu & Zhou
entries.text: # Lahanis, Liu & Zhou A Glucksman Fellowship study at NYU Stern comparing trading strategies including online portfolio selection. Its frictionless ranking is the claim stress-tested in [[Costs kill mean reversion]]. Their work, credited; not mine.

entries.title: Research note · 04_REFERENCES/Li & Hoi survey
entries.text: # Li & Hoi survey Bin Li and Steven C. H. Hoi, "Online Portfolio Selection: A Survey", *ACM Computing Surveys* (2014). Defines UCRP, EG, PAMR, OLMAR and BCRP as used in [[OPS replication]].

entries.title: Research note · 04_REFERENCES/Politis & Romano 1994
entries.text: # Politis & Romano 1994 Dimitris N. Politis and Joseph P. Romano, "The Stationary Bootstrap", *Journal of the American Statistical Association* (1994). Method behind [[Block bootstrap Monte Carlo]].

entries.title: Research note · README
entries.text: # Research vault Open this folder in [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) (free) to browse it as a graph. The portfolio builds its knowledge graph from these same files at build time, so a note added here appears on the site after the next deploy. - `00_CORE_THESES/` — the claims I am testing - `01_DATA_PIPELINES/` — where the data comes from and what it leaves out - `02_MODELS_AND_SIMULATIONS/` — backtests, Monte Carlo and valuation models - `03_PEER_REVIEW_LOGS/` — what I got wrong and how it was fixed - `04_REFERENCES/` — papers and prior work Link with `[[Note name]]`. Tag in the front matter. Every number in a note must come from a script or a model in the repository, never typed from memory.
